label: Air fryer

questions.text: How many times a week is it used?
questions.why: Heavy use wears the heating element and fan.

questions.text: Is the basket cleaned after each use?
questions.why: Old grease can smoke and burn.

questions.text: Is there space around the back where the hot air comes out?
Where does it stand while in use?
questions.why: It gets hot underneath and behind.

questions.text: Do you use paper or foil liners?
questions.why: Loose liners can touch the heater.

questions.text: Have you noticed smoke, a burning smell or it not heating?
questions.why: Early signs let you get it checked before a small fault grows.

care_tips.text: Unplug the air fryer and let it cool before cleaning it.
care_tips.why: It stays hot and is live while plugged in.

care_tips.text: Don't open the air fryer yourself; leave repairs to the brand's authorised service.
care_tips.why: Inside there are live parts, and opening it can also end the warranty.

care_tips.text: Don't bypass or tamper with the thermostat or any safety cut-out.
care_tips.why: These stop the appliance overheating; without them it can cause burns or a fire.

care_tips.text: Clean the basket and tray after each use.
care_tips.why: Old grease can smoke and burn.

care_tips.text: Keep space around the back and sides.
Use only liners your manual allows, and never let them cover the heater.
If it smokes or smells of burning, unplug it and contact the brand's service.
care_tips.why: These can be signs of a fault.

reminders.text: Deep-clean the air fryer's basket and tray (unplugged and cool).
reminders.interval_text: about every 2 weeks with regular use
reminders.note: Check your manual for the interval for your model.
